paper_title: Immunodiagnostic plasma amino acid residue biomarkers detect cancer early and predict treatment response
prediction_task: Multi-cancer early detection from plasma amino acid biomarkers + CDKi treatment response prediction

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Most cancers are advanced stage (e.g., PDAC all but 1 are stage III-IV). Utility for multi-cancer 'early' detection is unclear and not supported by provided data. Title claims early detection but data is mostly late-stage.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Revised to clarify limitations of staging distribution and added subgroup analysis by stage.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Cohort size is too small to make any definitive conclusions regarding utility of the test for MCED or for predicting response to treatment (N=92 for cancer detection, N=30 for drug response).
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Acknowledged power limitation and framed as proof-of-concept.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Age distributions among cases and controls appear quite different. Is there an association between biomarker values and age/sex? Were patients fasted when blood was collected? Important confounders not assessed.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added age/sex-adjusted analysis and fasting status reporting.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Although authors include autoimmune and infection controls, other benign conditions pertinent to the field of cancer detection are missing.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added discussion of benign condition controls as future work.

reviewer_strengths.text: Identification of immunodiagnostic biomarkers is very novel. Very sophisticated data analysis. Results are significant and the study is state-of-the-art.
